chrome.tabs reference page

chrome.scripting

Use the chrome.scripting API to execute script in different contexts. The API requires the scripting permission and host access to the target tab, either persistent or temporary through activeTab.

Permissions

To use the scripting API, declare the "scripting" permission in the manifest plus host permissions for the pages you inject into. Alternatively, rely on the activeTab permission granted by a user gesture.

Methods

executeScript injects a script into a target context. The script runs once, returns a serializable result per frame, and cannot close over variables from the calling extension context.

Limitations

Injected functions are serialized before injection, so they lose their closure. Arguments must be JSON-serializable and results are structured-clone compatible values only.
